name: ntier-spine-leaf
description: N-tier placement over a routed link graph: two compute nodes reach two memory pools through a leaf-spine fabric (pool-b hangs off the leaf, pool-a off the spine). Spill destinations are policy-chosen (nearest-with-space default), peer locals are spill candidates, and each transfer occupies every hop link plus the switches it crosses plus the destination tier.
assumptions: Local capacity is 2 GiB per node to force remote traffic; this exercises placement, not a deployment configuration.
Link, switch, and tier latencies/bandwidths are class assumptions, not measurements.
Routing is static shortest-path; congestion does not reroute (see ROADMAP deferred items).
Placement is single-owner: no replication, no coherence protocol.
The workload is synthetic KV-cache decode, not a captured trace.
